subject: Helio POC: recommended model slate + commercial impact and next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@helio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Helio POC: recommended model slate + commercial impact and next steps

Lucy — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our demo + hands-on review and a recommended shortlist so your team can pick the direction for the POC. I kept this focused on three candidate routes (tradeoffs below) and an operational checklist to avoid early regressions.

Recommended shortlist (high level)
- Redwood-S-quant (our optimized INT8 variant) — best cost/latency balance for 95% of generative chat and summarization workloads.
  - p95 latency (512 tokens): ~120ms on g5.2x / ~210ms on cheaper vCPUs with batching
  - cost: ~$0.35 / 1M tokens (in hosted configuration)
  - quality: near-baseline vs fp16 on instruction-following, small degradation on long hallucination-prone prompts

- OpenLM-Fast32 (large-feedforward, lower latency) — strong for short-answer extraction and reranking.
  - p95 latency (256 tokens): ~85ms
  - cost: ~$0.50 / 1M tokens
  - quality: excellent for QA/rerank; weaker on open-ended creative summarization

- Mistral-Compact-Q4 (quantized, small context overhead) — lowest cost path for high volume inference with acceptable quality for templated responses.
  - p95 latency (512 tokens): ~180ms
  - cost: ~$0.18 / 1M tokens
  - quality: slightly lower ROUGE for abstractive summarization, good for rule-constrained outputs

Key tradeoffs we noticed during the hands-on:
- Latency vs cost: Redwood-S-quant is the best middle ground. If Helio expects many short-turn interactions (<=128 tokens) OpenLM-Fast32 wins on latency but increases unit cost.
- Quality regression risk: Mistral-Compact-Q4 and aggressive quantization show higher variance on long-context summarization and instruction-follow prompts — recommend a regression gate for any prompt set changes.
- Operational controls: we can enable automatic fallback (to fp16 or to a higher-quality variant) per-route, and set a canary rollout to validate prompts before broad traffic.

Included: benchmark CSV (summary + raw), the prompt_set_v1 we used for scoring, and the short prompt-regression checklist. Links below and attachments.

Proposed next steps (two-week cadence):
1) Run a 24–48 hour POC using Helio sample traffic (we'll provide a sandbox key). Estimated run window: Apr 24–26. Goal: validate latency distributions and end-to-end cost for 50M tokens/month projection.
2) We build a focused regression test (5 golden prompts + 3 adversarial prompts) — we recommend this gate be required for any model or quantization change.
3) Commercial path: if POC matches SLA, Marissa will follow up with a Dedicated pool term (reserve estimate + burst pricing).

Links: benchmark folder (drive), HubSpot deal (I attached a short playbook).

Questions for you: is Apr 24–26 a good window for a short-run POC? Also — can you confirm whether procurement will need an initial NDA or a full Master Services Agreement before we share the sandbox credentials?

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_results_v2.csv; prompt_set_v1.jsonl

Thanks, Evelyn — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications from eng:
1) For the Redwood-S-quant numbers, how much of the cost delta vs Mistral-Compact-Q4 is from model size vs runtime kernel efficiency? In other words, is the $/1M tokens primarily driven by lower op count, or by better batching and kernel selection?
2) For the 50M tokens/month projection, can you provide a ballpark total monthly spend per model on the shortlist? Procurement also asked whether our data will be retained in the hosted sandbox during the POC (we're fine with a short retention window if needed).

Happy to make the Apr 24–26 window work if you need it.

—Lucy
Director of Product, Helio

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@helio.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helio POC: recommended model slate + commercial impact and next steps

Lucy — quick answers to your questions:
- Cost drivers: for Redwood-S-quant the delta vs Mistral-Compact-Q4 is mainly runtime and kernel efficiency (our fused attention + KV cache paths) + batching. Mistral-Compact is smaller which helps, but Redwood-S-quant benefits from inference-time kernel scheduling that reduces per-token op cost at typical Helio sequence distributions.

- Ballpark spend (50M tokens/month, hosted):
  - Redwood-S-quant: ~$17.5k / month (includes automatic caching assumptions — 7% effective token saving from prefix cache)
  - OpenLM-Fast32: ~$25k / month
  - Mistral-Compact-Q4: ~$9k / month

Notes: numbers assume default batching (100ms batching window) and average output length of 320 tokens per request. We can change batching/latency knobs to tune cost vs p95. If you want Dedicated pools the unit economics shift (we can provide a reserve vs burst quote once we have throughput numbers).

- Data retention in sandbox: by default sandbox logs are retained for 7 days. We can shorten retention or enable a customer-managed retention policy for the POC; we will not share logs outside the Helio project. If procurement needs an MSA/NDA before credentials, we can pause the sandbox share until that's signed.

Action items I can take immediately: run a dry gauge on Helio sample corpus to estimate real-world batching gains; schedule a 24-hour full-run POC; and prepare a canary rollout plan that will produce a short evaluation report (latency, token cost, 10 golden prompt pass/fail).

Attached: short-run-estimate.csv (benchmark snippet). I'll also seed the prompt regression harness with the prompt_set_v1 you saw in the attachments.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_results_v2.csv (snippet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Team — wrapping this up internally so we have clear commercial and technical owners.

Marissa: can you please start the procurement thread with Helio (procurement@helio.com) and attach the SLA-draft-Helio.docx I included? Ask whether they prefer an NDA first or MSA; either is fine but call out that sandbox keys are available after the initial paperwork. Also include a rough Dedicated reserve estimate based on Karthik's spend numbers (we'll need a 6–12 month commit option).

Karthik: please schedule the 24-hour POC for Apr 24–25 using Helio sample corpus (Lucy confirmed the window). Use Redwood-S-quant as the default route and run Mistral-Compact-Q4 in parallel on a small fraction (10%) of traffic to compare live regression characteristics. Produce a short report (1 page) covering p95 latency, token cost, and 5-prompt regression pass/fail.

Risk/guardrails to call out to Helio:
- Any prompt change that increases abstraction or asks for multi-document synthesis should be gated behind the prompt regression harness.
- If hallucination rates increase >3% on golden prompts, auto-fallback to OpenLM-Fast32 for those routes until we've tuned prompts.

Lucy — looping you so you're aware of owners. We'll aim to have the procurement note and POC schedule out by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
